proposed_widenings.name: on_sneak_attack_hit_trigger (class feature family)
proposed_widenings.justification: Cunning Strike fires when Sneak Attack damage is dealt — it is not a standalone activation. No existing ClassFeatureMechanics family has an on-hit trigger shape. The mastery 'on_hit_trigger' family covers weapon hits but is not usable for class features (different UnitRecord kind). A parallel family for class features is required.
proposed_widenings.evidence: When you deal Sneak Attack damage, you can add one of the following Cunning Strike effects.

proposed_widenings.name: dice_cost resource (forgo Sneak Attack damage dice)
proposed_widenings.justification: Each Cunning Strike effect costs 1d6 of Sneak Attack damage — the rogue removes those dice before rolling. This 'forgo N damage dice' pattern does not exist in any current resource atom. It is not use_count, action_quota, bonus_action_quota, or spell_slot.
proposed_widenings.evidence: Each effect has a die cost, which is the number of Sneak Attack damage dice you must forgo to add the effect. You remove the die before rolling.

proposed_widenings.name: menu_of_effects (choose one at use-time)
proposed_widenings.justification: Cunning Strike exposes a set of effects the rogue selects from each time the trigger fires. The current surface has no construct for 'pick one of N effects when activating'. ClassFeatureActivationMechanics has a single effect field; mastery effects are also singular.
proposed_widenings.evidence: you can add one of the following Cunning Strike effects

proposed_widenings.name: Condition: poisoned
proposed_widenings.justification: The Poison effect applies the Poisoned condition. The current Condition type only contains 'prone'. Poisoned must be added to the Condition union.
proposed_widenings.evidence: the target has the Poisoned condition for 1 minute

proposed_widenings.name: repeat_save (save at end of each of target's turns)
proposed_widenings.justification: The Poison effect includes a repeating save: 'At the end of each of its turns, the Poisoned target repeats the save, ending the effect on itself on a success.' This is a distinct resolution shape from the single save_gate atom — it is a persist+repeat_save lifecycle. Nothing in the current surface covers this.
proposed_widenings.evidence: At the end of each of its turns, the Poisoned target repeats the save, ending the effect on itself on a success.

proposed_widenings.name: size_constraint on save_gate (Large or smaller)
proposed_widenings.justification: The Trip effect only applies to targets that are Large or smaller. No current surface type allows a target-size predicate to gate whether the effect fires.
proposed_widenings.evidence: If the target is Large or smaller, it must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or have the Prone condition.

proposed_widenings.name: move effect for ClassFeatureEffect (Withdraw: half speed, no OA)
proposed_widenings.justification: The Withdraw effect grants movement (up to half Speed) without provoking Opportunity Attacks. Neither 'move' nor 'deny_opportunity_attack' (both v4 atoms) exist in the ClassFeatureEffect union. They would need to be added.
proposed_widenings.evidence: Immediately after the attack, you move up to half your Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

notes: Do NOT write content/rogue_cunning_strike_l5.dhall or .json — no honest encoding exists. Primary blocker is structural: the feature triggers off Sneak Attack damage (an on-hit event) rather than being a standalone activation, making ClassFeatureActivationMechanics a false fit. Secondary blockers — dice-cost resource, menu-of-effects, poisoned condition, repeat-save lifecycle, size constraint, movement effect — would require widenings even if a new trigger family were added. All three Cunning Strike options were assessed; each requires at least one of the secondary widenings.
